<summary>
  <para>Builds an <see cref="AsyncPolicy{TResult}"/> that functions as a circuit breaker.</para>
  <para>The circuit breaks if, within any timeslice lasting <paramref name="samplingDuration"/>, the proportion of actions resulting in a handled exception exceeds <paramref name="failureThreshold"/>, provided that at least <paramref name="minimumThroughput"/> actions pass through the circuit during the timeslice.</para>
  <para>The circuit remains broken for <paramref name="durationOfBreak"/>. Any attempt to execute this policy while the circuit is broken immediately throws a <see cref="BrokenCircuitException"/> containing the exception or result that broke the circuit.</para>
  <para>If the first action after the break duration results in a handled exception or result, the circuit breaks again for another <paramref name="durationOfBreak"/>. If no exception or handled result occurs, the circuit resets.</para>
</summary>
<param name="policyBuilder">The policy builder.</param>
<param name="failureThreshold">The failure threshold at which the circuit breaks. This value must be between 0 and 1; for example, 0.5 represents breaking the circuit when 50% or more of the actions result in a handled failure.</param>
<param name="samplingDuration">The duration of the timeslice over which failure ratios are assessed.</param>
<param name="minimumThroughput">The minimum throughput. This many actions or more must pass through the circuit during the timeslice for the statistics to be considered significant and the circuit breaker to act.</param>
<param name="durationOfBreak">The duration for which the circuit remains open before resetting.</param>
<param name="onBreak">The action to call when the circuit transitions to the <see cref="CircuitState.Open"/> state.</param>
<param name="onReset">The action to call when the circuit resets to the <see cref="CircuitState.Closed"/> state.</param>
<returns>The policy instance.</returns>
<remarks>See <c>Release It!</c> by Michael T. Nygard.</remarks>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">Thrown for <c>failureThreshold</c> when its value is not greater than zero.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">Thrown for <c>failureThreshold</c> when its value is greater than one.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">Thrown for <c>samplingDuration</c> when its value is less than the minimum resolution of the circuit breaker timer.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">Thrown for <c>minimumThroughput</c> when its value is not greater than one.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">Thrown for <c>durationOfBreak</c> when its value is not greater than zero.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentNullException">Thrown when <c>onBreak</c> is null.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentNullException">Thrown when <c>onReset</c> is null.</exception>

<summary>
  <para>Builds a <see cref="Policy" /> that functions like a circuit breaker.</para>
  <para>The circuit breaks if, within any time slice of duration <paramref name="samplingDuration" />, the proportion of actions resulting in a handled exception exceeds <paramref name="failureThreshold" />, provided that the number of actions passing through the circuit in the time slice is at least <paramref name="minimumThroughput" />.</para>
  <para>The circuit remains open for <paramref name="durationOfBreak" />. Any attempt to execute this policy while the circuit is open immediately throws a <see cref="BrokenCircuitException" /> containing the exception that caused the circuit to break.</para>
  <para>If the first action after the break duration results in a handled exception, the circuit opens again for another <paramref name="durationOfBreak" />. If no exception is thrown, the circuit resets.</para>
</summary>
<param name="policyBuilder">The policy builder.</param>
<param name="failureThreshold">The failure threshold at which the circuit breaks (a number between 0 and 1; for example, 0.5 represents breaking if 50% or more of actions result in a handled failure).</param>
<param name="samplingDuration">The duration of the time slice over which failure ratios are assessed.</param>
<param name="minimumThroughput">The minimum throughput: this many actions or more must pass through the circuit in the time slice for the statistics to be considered significant and the circuit breaker to come into action.</param>
<param name="durationOfBreak">The duration for which the circuit remains open before resetting.</param>
<param name="onBreak">The action to call when the circuit transitions to the <see cref="CircuitState.Open" /> state.</param>
<param name="onReset">The action to call when the circuit resets to the <see cref="CircuitState.Closed" /> state.</param>
<param name="onHalfOpen">The action to call when the circuit transitions to the <see cref="CircuitState.HalfOpen" /> state and is ready to try action executions again.</param>
<returns>The policy instance.</returns>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">failureThreshold; The value must be greater than zero.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">failureThreshold; The value must be less than or equal to one.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">samplingDuration; The value must be equal to or greater than the minimum resolution of the CircuitBreaker timer.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">minimumThroughput; The value must be greater than one.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">durationOfBreak; The value must be greater than zero.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentNullException">onBreak</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentNullException">onReset</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentNullException">onHalfOpen</exception>
<remarks>(See <c>Release It!</c> by Michael T. Nygard.)</remarks>

  <para>The circuit opens when <paramref name="exceptionsAllowedBeforeBreaking"/> consecutive exceptions handled by this policy are raised.</para>

<returns>The policy instance.</returns>

<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">Thrown when exceptionsAllowedBeforeBreaking is not greater than zero.</exception>

<summary>
  <para>Builds a <see cref="Policy" /> that functions as a circuit breaker.</para>
  <para>The circuit breaks if, during any time slice with a duration of <paramref name="samplingDuration" />, the proportion of actions that result in a handled exception exceeds <paramref name="failureThreshold" />, provided that the number of actions passing through the circuit during the time slice is at least <paramref name="minimumThroughput" />.</para>
  <para>The circuit remains broken for <paramref name="durationOfBreak" />. Any attempt to execute this policy while the circuit is broken immediately throws a <see cref="BrokenCircuitException" /> containing the exception that broke the circuit.</para>
  <para>If the first action after the break duration results in a handled exception, the circuit breaks again for another <paramref name="durationOfBreak" />. If no exception is thrown, the circuit resets.</para>
</summary>
<param name="policyBuilder">The policy builder.</param>
<param name="failureThreshold">The failure threshold at which the circuit breaks. This value must be between 0 and 1; for example, 0.5 represents breaking the circuit when 50% or more of the actions result in a handled failure.</param>
<param name="samplingDuration">The duration of the time slice over which failure ratios are assessed.</param>
<param name="minimumThroughput">The minimum throughput. This many actions or more must pass through the circuit during the time slice for the statistics to be considered significant and the circuit breaker to act.</param>
<param name="durationOfBreak">The duration for which the circuit remains open before resetting.</param>
<param name="onBreak">The action to call when the circuit transitions to the <see cref="CircuitState.Open" /> state.</param>
<param name="onReset">The action to call when the circuit resets to the <see cref="CircuitState.Closed" /> state.</param>
<param name="onHalfOpen">The action to call when the circuit transitions to the <see cref="CircuitState.HalfOpen" /> state and is ready to try action executions again.</param>
<returns>The policy instance.</returns>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">failureThreshold;The value must be greater than zero.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">failureThreshold;The value must be less than or equal to one.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">samplingDuration;The value must be equal to or greater than the minimum resolution of the CircuitBreaker timer.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">minimumThroughput;The value must be greater than one.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">durationOfBreak;The value must be greater than zero.</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentNullException">onBreak</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentNullException">onReset</exception>
<exception cref="ArgumentNullException">onHalfOpen</exception>
<remarks>See <c>Release It!</c> by Michael T. Nygard.</remarks>

<summary>

  <para>The circuit breaks when <paramref name="exceptionsAllowedBeforeBreaking"/> consecutive exceptions handled by this policy are raised.</para>
  <para>The circuit remains broken for <paramref name="durationOfBreak"/>. Any attempt to execute this policy while the circuit is broken immediately throws a <see cref="BrokenCircuitException"/> containing the exception that broke the circuit.</para>

<remarks>(See “Release It!” by Michael T. Nygard.)</remarks>
<exception cref="ArgumentOutOfRangeException">exceptionsAllowedBeforeBreaking; the value must be greater than zero.</exception>
